body.p: Applicant submits this Reply in response to the Office Action mailed on July 28, 2017.
Claims 1-20 are currently pending in this application. By this Amendment,

Applicant amends claims 1, 3, 9, 11, 17, and 19 The originally filed specification and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended claims, for example, at paragraph [035]. Applicant believes that this Amendment adds no new matter.
Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the pending rejections for at least the reasons that follow.

Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection of claims 1-20, which were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Taylor to (U.S. Publication No. 2012/0041318 Al) ("Taylor)" in view of T. Mabotuwana et al. ("A model of blood flow in the mesenteric arterial system" Biomed Eng Online. 2007) ("Mabotuwana").
Page 4 of the Office Action interprets "blood flow demand" as referring to

"baseline (resting) mean blood flow." To further clarify the claims and distinguish the claim features from cited references, Applicant amends the claims to recite, "determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel based on the determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel and a physiological state of the patient, wherein the blood flow demand depends on the patient's physiological state; [and] calculating, using the determined blood flow demand, a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel via collateralized vasculature

supplying blood to the patient's bowel." In particular, the amendment, "wherein the blood flow demand depends on the patient's physiological state" precludes the interpretation of "blood flow demand" as referring to "baseline (resting) mean blood flow." Neither Taylor nor Mabotuwana, individually or in combination, would have rendered obvious the above-recited subject matter.

For the reasons discussed, Applicant submits that claims 1-20 are allowable over all of the cited references. Accordingly, Applicant requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the Section 103 rejections.

In the Office Action, claims 1-20 were provisionally rejected under the doctrine of obviousness-type double patenting over claims 21-40 of copending U.S. Application No. 15/080,829. U.S. Application No. 15/080,829 was abandoned as of a Notice of Abandonment mailed April 19, 2017. Without conceding to the assertions in the double patenting rejections, Applicant requests that the Examiner hold the double patenting rejections in abeyance until such time as no other issues remain in the application, and the pending claims are deemed otherwise allowable. At that time, Applicant will investigate the need for any terminal disclaimers.

The Office Action contains characterizations of the claims and the related art with which the applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.
In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to be
understood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any

exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.
Applicant respectfully requests that this Reply under 37 C.F.R. § 1.116 be

entered by the Examiner, placing the claims in condition for allowance. The proposed claim amendments do not raise new issues or necessitate the undertaking of any additional search of the art by the Examiner. Therefore, this Reply should allow for immediate action by the Examiner.
Furthermore, Applicant respectfully points out that the final Office Action

presented new arguments as to the application of the art against the pending claims. It is respectfully submitted that the entering of this Reply would allow Applicant to respond to the final rejection and place the application in condition for allowance.
Finally, Applicant submits that the entry of this Reply would place the application in better form for appeal, should the Examiner dispute the patentability of the pending claims.

In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
If the examiner believes a telephone conversation might advance prosecution, the examiner is invited to call applicant's undersigned representative at 202-803-8075.
Please grant any extensions of time required to enter this response and charge any additional required fees to Deposit Account No. 50-5906. In addition, the
Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees due and any other fees due under 37 C.F.R. § 1.16 or § 1.17 during the pendency of this application to Deposit Account No. 50-5906.
Respectfully submitted, BOOKOFF McANDREWS, PLLC
